blocks.text: A household can be above the annual income poverty threshold and still lack a financial cushion. Asset poverty compares net worth with a three-month poverty-level benchmark; liquid asset poverty uses the provider’s defined assets that can be converted to cash. These are household measures, so their percentages cannot be added to population poverty rates.

In the provider’s source-labelled 2021 data, 20% of Ohio households are asset poor and 29% are liquid asset poor. The corresponding US estimates are 19% and 27%. These are descriptive source estimates, not measurements of current 2026 conditions or tests of a statistically significant difference.

blocks.text: The editable dataset preserves every original provider precision field and the exact statistical response. It does not convert those fields into a confidence interval without an explicit confidence level and unit. Bars show the selected point estimates.

sections.title: Household asset history with explicit gaps

blocks.text: The received trend includes published observations for 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2019 and 2021. For 2017, 2018 and 2020, the source returns an unavailable or suppressed marker. The tables preserve those empty rate cells; they are not zero values and have not been interpolated.

Source years identify the provider’s editions. The measures concern households and differ from the annual income-poverty and five-year county datasets elsewhere in this report. Descriptive changes in these displayed estimates do not establish a cause or statistical significance.

sections.summary: Retained issuer transcription and original provider values

blocks.text: The working edition uses the original provider history. For Ohio 2015 asset poverty, that response is 28.9%, while the retained report transcription reads 28.2%. For Ohio 2019, the original provider value is 27.0%; the OCR transcription is corrupted. Both representations remain attached to the editable source so the issuer’s original page can be reviewed before its text is changed.

The issuer’s tables also contain 2011 observations, but 2011 is absent from the received provider trend selection. Those old cells remain in the transcription concordance and are not reconstructed in the provider working dataset.

The provider’s explanatory copy includes a four-person 2020 threshold example. The definition chapter preserves that date rather than relabelling the example as 2021 or 2026. Local modeled estimates are outside this Ohio/US source selection.
